hook: The greatest Ottoman architect, who built over 300 buildings.

pages.x: Sinan was born around 1490 in a Christian village near Kayseri, in Anatolia. As a young man he was taken in the levy of Christian boys for the sultan's service, became a Muslim, and trained as a carpenter and soldier in the Janissaries, the elite infantry.
As an army engineer he built bridges, boats and forts on campaigns from Persia to Hungary, once putting up a bridge over the Danube in just 13 days.
In 1538, at about 48, he became the empire's chief architect. Over the next 50 years he designed more than 300 buildings: mosques, schools, hospitals, bridges, baths and aqueducts.
For Sultan Suleiman he built the Süleymaniye Mosque, finished in 1557, crowning a hill above the Golden Horn. He placed his own small, plain tomb just outside its walls.
At about 80, in Edirne, he built the Selimiye Mosque, its great dome resting on eight pillars and framed by four slender minarets 70 metres tall. He called it his masterpiece.

A legend says Sinan loved Mihrimah, Suleiman's daughter, and built her two mosques on either side of Istanbul. On her birthday, the story goes, the sun sets behind the minaret of one as the moon rises over the other.
Sinan is the greatest architect of the Ottoman Empire, often compared with Michelangelo. His mosques still shape the skyline of Istanbul, and his pupils built the Blue Mosque.
pts: Built the Süleymaniye and Selimiye mosques
